data.one_liner: An event bus library to dispatch and listen to events across your app using Dart streams.
data.what_it_does: Provides a simple event hub mechanism to fire events and register listeners globally without needing dedicated event classes. It uses underlying Dart streams to communicate between decoupled components.
use_when: You need a simple event bus to decouple components across your application.
You want to avoid defining custom event classes or heavy state management for simple messaging.
You need to dispatch events from anywhere and listen anywhere.
avoid_when: You need robust, typed state management with predictable state trees and debugging tools.
Your architecture benefits more from strict unidirectional data flows or inherited widgets.
strengths: Extremely simple API with minimal boilerplate.
No need to define dedicated event classes.
Works across all Dart and Flutter platforms.
weaknesses: Relies on dynamic data types for event payloads.
Global event buses can lead to untraceable code paths if overused.
